Subject: Renewal proposal — term swap + phased capacity uplift

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Brightbeat is prepared to move forward on a renewal but with two asks before we sign:

1) Term swap: We want to shift from the 24-month term you proposed to a 12+12 (auto renew) arrangement with the option to terminate at 12 months with 60 days' notice.
2) Phased capacity uplift: We'll start with the current committed baseline and add +30% capacity for months 1–6, then +60% for months 7–12. We'd like pricing clarity for both tranches and how overage billing will behave during the ramp.

Can you send proposed redlines to the MSA and a new order form reflecting the two tranches? If legal could also call out any data-retention or audit-impact changes that come with the term swap, that would help our GC.

Attached: Brightbeat_internal_capacity.xlsx (customer-side forecast).

Best,

Brightbeat Inc.

David / team — quick legal read and asks attached. Summary of primary redlines I suggest: 

1) Term language: Implement 12+12 auto-renewal with a 60-day opt-out. Add a carve-out clarifying that any prepaid credits tied to the 24-month pricing will be reconciled pro rata on early termination.
2) Order form pricing: Add explicit table for tranche pricing and a defined calculation for overage during the ramp (we should cap overage rate at 150% list for months in-tranche).
3) Audit & data retention: Do not change default retention in the MSA; instead add a clause stating customer may request accelerated logs for audits at customer expense.
4) Change management: Require a 10-business-day notice for any tranche increases beyond the committed +60% uplift.

Open question for contracts: Brightbeat wants the opt-out at 12 months — we should confirm if they expect any prorated refund of prepayments or a credit arrangement. If they insist on guaranteed refund language we should push to credit offset only.

I've attached an annotated MSA_redline_20280809.docx (track changes) and a redline PDF of OrderForm_v3.pdf. I recommend we call Wilson & Park (their counsel) to walk through the MSA carve-outs before sending final.

— Marissa Cole
